title: ARWP Search Platform Eligibility
purpose: Prevent agents from applying platform-specific Search tactics to sites, scopes or deployment modes that are not eligible for them. This layer is an applicability/configuration gate, not a ranking score.

rules.claim: Google Preferred Sources accepts domain-level and subdomain-level sites, not a subdirectory as an independently selectable source.
rules.decision: Require hostname-root scope before recommending a Preferred Sources CTA. Keep subdirectory sites search-eligible, but do not pretend that the path itself can be selected as a Preferred Source.

rules.claim: Google Indexing API can only be used for pages containing JobPosting or BroadcastEvent embedded in a VideoObject.
rules.decision: Do not recommend or call Google Indexing API for ordinary articles, documentation, product pages or generic site updates.

rules.claim: Next.js metadataBase composes relative canonical, alternate and other URL-based metadata into absolute URLs.
rules.decision: For a known production site root, require metadataBase to resolve to that same public root or record an explicit review when metadata is fully absolute.

rules.claim: Next.js basePath is the framework control for deploying an application under a domain sub-path and is inlined at build time.
rules.decision: When the public site root is a subdirectory, require an exact basePath match and rebuild after basePath changes. Do not substitute assetPrefix for application routing scope.

rules.claim: Next.js static export does not support features that require a Node.js server or dynamic request-time behavior, including several dynamic-route, request, rewrite, redirect, header, proxy, ISR, default image optimization and Server Action patterns.
rules.decision: Before deploying output: export to static hosting, inventory server-dependent features and fail the gate when any required feature cannot be computed at build time.

rules.claim: GitHub Pages can publish from a branch or a custom GitHub Actions workflow; with custom Actions the uploaded Pages artifact is the publication boundary, while a repository CNAME file is not proof of the active custom-domain configuration.
rules.decision: Verify the actual Pages publishing mode and final artifact before treating repository files as production Search evidence.
